long_description.before:
Artificial Societies are networks of thousands of AIs that model the opinions of important groups of people. We are informing clients with $3T+ in total market cap, helping global F100 enterprises test how their biggest decisions shift the opinions that matter, including those of their customers, investors, opinion leaders, and regulators.

We are experts in human societies. James, our Founder and CEO, is a Cambridge psychologist and data scientist who led the seminal paper that studied how 33,000 AI chatbots interact. Patrick, our Founder and Chief Product Officer, is an Applied Behavioural Scientist with years of experience helping F500 enterprises conduct market research. They are joined by a team of behavioural scientists, social scientists, and political scientists, all with a passion for uniting technology and an understanding of humanity.

Our vision of Artificial Societies is a Societal World Model - socially intelligent technology that shape the decisions that shape the world. No planes fly without a wind-tunnel; no medicines are approved without clinical trials; and yet, the biggest decision societies face today are taken as bets. We see Artificial Societies as a historically inevitable technology, and see it as our lives' mission to bring it to life.
long_description.after:
Simulate decisions that matter.

Artificial Societies builds a foundational model of human societies so enterprises and sovereigns can explore how people may respond before making consequential decisions. We combine behavioural science with simulations grounded in real-world behaviour to understand individual perspectives and how opinions develop across connected groups.

Teams use our simulations to test communications, prepare for crises, explore new markets, and assess investor and public-policy reactions. They can run surveys, focus groups, interviews and experiments with simulated audiences, including stakeholders who are difficult to reach through traditional research, and decisions too sensitive to test otherwise.

Our mission is to pioneer socially intelligent technology that shape the decisions that shape the world.

one_liner.before: We build networks of AIs to simulate high-value audiences
one_liner.after: Foundational model of human societies for consequential decisions

long_description.before: Edge AI is inevitable, but shipping it is painful: every device class behaves differently, runtimes vary, models are huge, and performance collapses under memory/power constraints. RunAnywhere turns that into an enterprise-ready workflow: one SDK to run models on-device, plus a control plane to manage models, enforce policies, and measure outcomes across thousands of devices.
long_description.after: RunAnywhere runs open-weight models at full speed wherever a company needs them. Wally is our inference stack for open models: serverless inference, BYOC, or on-prem, so code and data never leave their network. One command puts a Wally-served model inside Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness, OpenCode, Hermes, OpenClaw, etc. When a model fits on the device, the same tooling runs it locally through our open-source SDKs for iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux, and web, built on kernels written by our agentic harness for Apple and Qualcomm silicon (10K+ GitHub stars).

one_liner.before: The default way of running on-device AI at Scale
one_liner.after: Fastest inference anywhere: open models on-prem, hosted or on-device

long_description.before:
Archer is the financial infrastructure for the AI data economy.

We’re building global payouts, stablecoin banking, and yield infrastructure for the companies supplying data to frontier AI labs.

As demand for high-quality data grows, millions of contributors around the world are generating, labeling, validating, and improving the datasets that power modern AI systems. Yet the financial infrastructure behind these platforms remains slow, fragmented, and expensive.

Archer enables data marketplaces, AI labor platforms, and reinforcement learning environment providers to onboard workers globally, pay contributors instantly, and earn yield on idle balances.

Today, companies use Archer to manage contributor earnings, global payouts, and treasury operations across hundreds of countries and payment corridors.

We believe the next generation of AI companies will need purpose-built financial infrastructure. Just as cloud providers became the backbone of software, Archer is building the financial layer for the global workforce powering artificial intelligence.
long_description.after:
We believe AI will be one of humanity’s next great masterpieces. Building it will require financial infrastructure as ambitious as the companies creating it. We're founders backed by Y Combinator building the financial rails underpinning the AI data economy.

Masterpiece provides short term working capital to data vendors that sell training data, evaluation work, and reinforcement learning environments to frontier AI labs.

A major financing gap exists in this market. Data vendors often need to pay contributors and fund operations before a lab has completed QA, accepted the work, and paid the invoice. This creates a 30 to 90 day cash gap between when vendors incur costs and when they receive payment. Legacy invoice lenders have little visibility into how to underwrite these assets.

Masterpiece closes that gap by advancing capital against high quality lab contracts and invoices. Vendors can use the capital to scale delivery, pay contributors, and fund growth, then repay masterpiece when the lab payment arrives.

one_liner.before: Global payouts for the workforce powering AI
one_liner.after: Working capital for data companies training frontier AI

long_description.before:
Nobody's built truly proactive AI, because it requires running inference on your entire life. In the cloud, that's insanely expensive and a privacy nightmare. But not on your own chip.

Every night, Sentient's on-device LLM wakes your Mac and understands what's new in your life (email, messages, files, Granola transcripts...), entirely locally, and distills it into a knowledge base.

You wake up to your work already prepared: the reply you forgot, drafted from your own context; the subscription you never use renewing tomorrow, caught; the report you promised in the group chat, ready to send. Everything is one click from firing through computer use, and nothing fires until you click.

Or click your Mac notch anytime and say "finish this for me." Sidekick takes over the thing you were doing with its own cursor while you move on.

On-device inference at this scale was supposed to be impossible: devices too slow, and models too dumb. So we built the stack ourselves: a custom LiteRT-LM fork (KV-cache reuse, speculative decoding, custom k-quants) that runs nightly on 8 GB Macs. The user's hardware does ~90% of the compute, and their own ChatGPT or Claude subscription does the rest, so our marginal cost is ~$0, and our servers store nothing.

We soft-launched late July with one Reddit post: top of r/macapps, 2,000+ users in 48 hours, $0 marketing. Free and open source for consumers; the same engine on the work stack (Slack, Granola, Linear, Notion) becomes the enterprise business.

Sentient OS raised ~$1M in pre-seed, backed by YC, Afore, and the a16z Speedrun scout fund.

long_description.before:
Mirrors provides regression testing for AI agents.

Teams shipping agents constantly change prompts, models, and tools, and there's no way to test any of it. Agents call bespoke internal tools and APIs no test framework can reproduce, so most teams ship on vibes.

Mirrors rebuilds the tools your agent calls from your own production traces, then replays real sessions against every change before it merges. You see which tool calls changed, which arguments moved, and where state landed differently. And when something fails, we tell you whether your agent regressed or something upstream moved.

Built for teams whose agents take irreversible actions. Refunds, record updates, outbound email.

Runs in your CI on every PR.
long_description.after:
Your agent worked fine yesterday. Today it loops, drops context, or calls a tool with the wrong arguments, and you find out from a user.

Teams shipping AI agents change prompts, models, and tools constantly, and the same failures keep coming back in production: context loss, loops, broken tool calls, regressions after a refactor.

Mirrors learns from your agent's production traces. It captures what worked and what failed in real sessions, then delivers the fix at runtime. Instead of waiting for someone to notice a regression and patch it by hand, the fix is applied automatically, so the same error never happens twice.

Built for teams whose agents do things they can't undo, like issuing refunds, updating customer records, or sending outbound email.

one_liner.before: Catch and fix AI agent regressions before they reach production
one_liner.after: Fix your AI agent's errors at runtime, so they never happen twice
